WITH patient_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    p.ID,
    p.SEX,
    AVG(l.ALB) - AVG(l.TP) as alb_minus_tp,
    AVG(l.APPT - l.PT) as avg_appt_minus_pt
  FROM Patient p
  INNER JOIN Laboratory l ON p.ID = l.ID
  GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX
),
sex_agg AS (
  SELECT 
    SEX,
    AVG(alb_minus_tp) as sex_avg_alb_minus_tp,
    AVG(avg_appt_minus_pt) as sex_avg_appt_minus_pt
  FROM patient_stats
  GROUP BY SEX
),
overall_mean_calc AS (
  SELECT AVG(sex_avg_appt_minus_pt) as overall_mean
  FROM sex_agg
),
filtered_sexes AS (
  SELECT 
    sex_avg_alb_minus_tp,
    sex_avg_appt_minus_pt
  FROM sex_agg
  WHERE sex_avg_appt_minus_pt > (SELECT overall_mean FROM overall_mean_calc)
)
SELECT 
  AVG(sex_avg_alb_minus_tp) as avg_alb_minus_tp,
  AVG(sex_avg_appt_minus_pt) as avg_appt_minus_pt,
  AVG(sex_avg_appt_minus_pt) - (SELECT overall_mean FROM overall_mean_calc) as exceeds_mean
FROM filtered_sexes

assumptions.assumption: For each patient, ALB is averaged independently over all its non-null values and TP is averaged independently over all its non-null values; these averages may be computed over different sets of laboratory records.
The per-test difference is computed as the average of (APPT - PT) for each test row, not as (average APPT) minus (average PT).

alternatives.interpretation: The average per-test difference is interpreted as the difference between the average APPT and average PT values, rather than the average of the row-level differences.
